Subject: Renewal + isolation request: PHI analytics enclave and temporary surge nodes

Hi Jasmine,

Hope youre well. Our renewal with Redwood is coming up (expires 2027-01-31) and were evaluating a configuration change: MedTech needs a PHI-isolated environment for analytics workloads (dedicated VPC/private enclave) plus the ability to burst additional clusters for a 12-week ramp during cutover. Primary asks:

- Can you provide a firm timeline and lead times for (a) a cloud-hosted private VPC enclave pinned to our account, and (b) an on-prem option if we go that route?
- High-level cost delta for reserved capacity + 12-week surge (ballpark is fine).
- Confirmation of what security evidence you can provide (SOC2 report, retention/audit logs, network diagram). Attached our security questionnaire for reference.
- Were considering extending the term from 12 -> 24 months if we can get staged capacity and price protection during the first renewal year — is that something Redwood supports?

Can we do a 30-minute kickoff next week to align on scope and SOW? ccd procurement and ops.

Thanks,
Sarah Choi
Head of Infrastructure, MedTech Inc

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Happy to run this with you. Quick answers up front and proposed next steps: 

- Timeline: cloud-hosted private VPC enclave (we manage control plane) typically: configuration + network validation = 3-4 weeks; provisioning and SLA pinning = additional 2-3 weeks (so 6-7 weeks total). On-prem installation (hardware + airgap options) runs longer: 10-12 weeks from PO due to hardware lead times and site validation.
- Pricing: ballpark for a dedicated PHI enclave + standard reserved commit is +25-35% vs current hosted spend depending on node sizing; 12-week surge (2x of baseline for analytics) is typically quoted as a short-term committed burst block (we can price as a one-time top-up or a timebound reserved delta). Ill include two scenarios in the SOW draft.
- Evidence: we can provide SOC 2 Type II summary, architecture/network diagram, audit log export guidance and a redacted runbook for data handling.

Next steps I propose:
1) Kickoff call (30 min) next Tue/Wed — agenda: capacity sizing, go/slow criteria, SOW path (amendment v new agreement), invoicing cadence.
2) Marcus will provide an ops matrix and target cutover timeline.
3) Ill circulate a SOW draft and a contract amendment template that folds in the 24-month option and surge pricing.

Ive attached a short SOW stub to get the conversation moving. Are mornings PST better for you?

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Hi Sarah / team — adding technical detail for the kickoff and ops planning. High-level matrix below; I attached the full ops workbook.

Summary:
- Cloud private VPC (managed control plane): 6-8 weeks to full readiness (network peering, SAML, KMS integration, test ingestion). Surge clusters: can be configured as hot standby pools; warm-up is ~3 days per pool depending on model footprints.
- On-prem appliance (airgap or hybrid): estimated 10-12 weeks; requires rack/cabinet power + on-site networking (well send hardware spec).
- Data isolation: PHI workloads will be logically separated by tenant with locked-down routing and dedicated GPU pools; audit logs retained per your retention policy (we can push raw logs to your secure bucket).
- Cutover approach (recommended): phased canary -> parallel run -> traffic switch over a 2-week window with surge pools used for parallel processing.

Pre-reqs we need from MedTech:
- Network CIDR and firewall contacts for peering/VPN validation
- Target weekly token throughput for analytics jobs during surge (example: 120M tokens/week)
- KMS provider and cert requirements for in-scope keys

Lead times: hardware spec attached; if you want hardware procurement managed through Redwood partners we can share an expedited path but that will change commercials slightly.

Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the details. A few procurement items we need clarified before we can sign the amendment: 

1) Term & price protection: wed like to convert to a 24-month contract with a fixed price schedule for the first 12 months (to protect against model-driven price variance). Are you able to provide a pricing table for 12- and 24-month options and the delta for the 12-week surge?
2) Invoicing cadence: we prefer quarterly invoicing for reserved capacity and a one-time invoice for the surge block. Can you accommodate?
3) SLA credits & cutover SLA exception: we need explicit SLA language for the cutover period (we understand there will be higher risk during traffic switch).

Please respond with proposed amendment language and a redline-ready SOW.

Hi all — thanks for the clear list of asks. Summarizing decisions and next steps so we can move to redline quickly: 

Decisions / agreement in principle:
- Term: Redwood will publish two commercial scenarios in the amendment: (A) 12-month renewal + 12-week surge (baseline uplift pricing), (B) 24-month renewal with staged capacity and a price-protection schedule for months 1-12. We will mark scenario B as the preferred path for discounting.
- Surge billing: one-time surge invoice (option to amortize across first two quarters if preferred by procurement).
- Cutover SLA: Redwood will include a cutover SLA exception clause with a documented rollback policy; non-cutover SLA breaches carry standard crediting.

Immediate next steps (today):
1) I attached the SOW draft for MTI (SOW-draft-MTI-Surge.docx) covering scope, surge sizing options, and cutover runbook.
2) Marcus: please add estimated node counts and a simple cost breakout for the two scenarios so procurement has a table to evaluate.
3) Neha (legal ops): Ive asked Neha to draft the amendment language that includes the term options and invoicing cadence. Neha, can you target a first-redline by 2026-12-29?
4) Proposed meeting to review redline and ops estimates: 2026-12-28 10:00 AM PST — invite to follow.

If that timeline works we can aim to have a signed amendment + SOW by mid-January to hit a February cutover window.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
